BURHAN:v4p266/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p266/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p266/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the second thumma in the repeated curse as making the second denunciation more emphatic than the first.
BURHAN:v4p266/r5.anchor: قلت الدلالة على إن الكرة الثانية من الدعاء ابلغ من الاولى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r4.claim: “This” refers to Qur’anic verses warning Quraysh about the Hereafter; the warning leaves them no excuse because the truth reached them in its ultimate form.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r4.anchor: The demonstrative pronoun “this” refers to those verses

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r5.claim: After the warning, each person is responsible for choosing the path to the Lord and His mercy or remaining in error and facing the outcome.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p27/r5.anchor: It was now the responsibility of the people.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.claim: The arrogant Quraysh leader fashioned a disdainfully delivered excuse, misjudging the Qur’an as a prophet’s stirring eloquence and ignoring its warning, though its statements are realities he will soon meet.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r2.anchor: they reckoned it to be a miracle of a prophet’s stirring and eloquent speech and never paid attention to its warning

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r1.claim: After pondering, he carefully weighed his opinion so that his words would take root with listeners and appear credible.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r1.anchor: he thoroughly weighed the opinion that came to his mind

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p45/r2.claim: The repeated curse before his verdict condemns both the hideous opinion and the foolish, self-important way he imagines a pebble to be a pearl.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r4.claim: The verb قتل may mean cursed or overcome; the phrase condemns an estimate that no rational person could make.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r4.anchor: فقتل كيف قدر، قتل: لعن، وقيل: غلب وقهر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r5.speaker: غير مسمى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r5.claim: Other explanations take the phrase as amazed praise of al-Walīd's original admiration for the Qurʾān, as praise for satisfying Quraysh, or as ironic praise; Abū Ḥayyān calls the view that it repeats the crowd's mockery far-fetched.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r6.claim: The rhetorical question how did he measure it? means how astonishing and strange his estimate was; Arabs use a curse-like formula when marveling at something exceptional.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p329#2/r6.anchor: وقولهم: قاتلهم الله، مشهور في كلام العرب أنه يقال عند استعظام الأمر والتعجب منه

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r2.claim: Here ‘qutila’ means ‘may he be cursed’; the same idiom occurs in 51:10.

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r1.claim: Qutila literally means he has been killed, or as an imprecation, may he be killed; Asad says a literal rendering is meaningless here.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r1.anchor: The expression qutila reads, literally, "he has been killed" or, as an imprecation, "may he be killed".

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r2.speaker: many commentators (Tabari among them)
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r2.claim: Many commentators, including Tabari, understand the expression as rejection from God's grace, a spiritual killing.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r2.anchor: many commentators (Tabari among them) understand it as signifying "he is rejected from God's grace" (lu'ina)

ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r3.claim: Asad renders it as self-destruction caused by the man's own action or attitude.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16#n9/r3.anchor: killed" spiritually by his own action or attitude; hence my rendering, "he destroys himself".

ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r1.claim: The curse can marvel at how accurately he guessed what Quraysh wanted him to say, like “May God fight them, how are they turned away?”
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r1.anchor: تعجيب من تقديره وإصابته في المخزورميه الغرض الذي كان ينتجيه قريش فهو نظير قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون

ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, it is sarcastic praise, using a curse idiom for someone whose excellence makes him an object of envy.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r2.anchor: أو ثناء عليه تهكما على نحو قاتله الله ما أشجعه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r3.claim: In Arabic, a curse such as “May God destroy him, how brave” can ironically mean that someone has reached an enviable degree of excellence; this phrase leans to the first interpretation, though for a different reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r3.anchor: فالعرب تقول قتله الله ما أشجعه وأخزاه الله ما أشعره يريدون أنه قد بلغ المبلغ الذي هو حقيق بأن يحسد

ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r4.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r4.claim: A report says Abū Jahl persuaded al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra to condemn the Qurʾān; al-Walīd first praised its unlike-anything quality, sweetness, beauty, fruitfulness, and supremacy, then called it transmitted magic after being pressed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r4.anchor: روي أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فقرأ عليه القرآن فكان رق له فبلغ ذلك أبا جهل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r5.speaker: محيي السنة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r5.claim: Muḥyī al-Sunna recounts that al-Walīd heard the Prophet recite 40:1–3, praised its sweetness and power, then Abu Jahl provoked him to deny it; al-Walīd called it magic learned from Musaylima and Babylonians.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p123#2/r5.anchor: وقال محيي السنة لما نزل على النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم حم تنزيل الكتاب من الله العزيز العليم إلى قوله تعالى المصير قام النبي

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r2.claim: The phrase may sarcastically express amazement at his calculation, or say he reached the utmost possible accusation, like the idiom wishing death on someone for astonishing bravery.
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:18-19/r2.anchor: تعجب من تقديره استهزاء به، أو لأنه أصاب أقصى ما يمكن أن يقال عليه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r3.claim: His thinking led others into ruin by barring faith, and brought him lasting destruction that deprived him of beneficial life in both worlds.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r3.anchor: تفكيره وتقديره قد أوقع غيره في الهلاك بمنعه من حياة الإيمان أصيب هو بما منعه من حياة نافعة في الدارين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r4.claim: The passive form declares his ruin, curse, and expulsion in this life as an invocation certain to be answered.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r4.anchor: بانيا للمفعول قوله مخبرا وداعيا دعاء مجابا لا يمكن تخلفه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r5.claim: The question expresses amazement at how he made this estimate; because it is invalid, even its manner deserves rejection.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p226/r5.anchor: معبرا بأداة الاستفهام إشارة إلى أنه مما يتعجب منه ويسأل عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r1.claim: The curse is an inserted exclamation between his devising and looking, branching into condemnation because his conduct warrants anger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r1.anchor: وهو إنشاء شتم مفرع على الإخبار عنه بأنه فكر وقدر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r2.claim: An interjected sentence can begin with fāʾ: interruption describes its placement, while the fāʾ still connects its meaning; the contrary grammatical objection is mistaken.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r2.anchor: والتفريع لا ينافي الاعتراض لأن الاعتراض وضع الكلام بين كلامين متصلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r3.claim: Qutila invokes a killer against him, wishing an end to his wretched life; the formula became a conventional expression of amazement or pity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the curse as a metonym for reaching a degree that makes the speaker envy him and wish him dead.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r4.anchor: وجعله الزمخشري كناية عن كونه بلغ مبلغا يحسده عليه المتكلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r5.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr rejects the envy reading: the phrase simply expresses amazement, and here condemns a conclusion that contradicted the man’s earlier denial that the Qur’an was magic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p308/r5.anchor: وأنا أحسب أن معنى الحسد غير ملحوظ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p406#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p406#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p406#2/r1.claim: Here fa-qutila means may he be cursed: how did he reckon it?

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r2.claim: The repeated phrase is an imprecation against al-Walid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p266/r2.anchor: {فقتل كيف قدر ثم قتل كيف قدر} دعاء عليه،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r1.claim: Qatada reports al-Walid’s judgment: the Quran was not poetry, had sweetness and brilliance, and rose above everything, yet he called it magic.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p267/r1.anchor: وقال قتادة: زعموا أنه قال: والله لقد نظرت فيما قال الرجل فإذا هو ليس بشعر، وإن له لحلاوة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r12.claim: One explanation takes the curse as repeated punishment: he was punished again and again.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r12.anchor: أي عوقب ثم عوقب , فيكون العقاب تكرر عليه مرة بعد أخرى

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r13.claim: Another explanation takes it as repeated cursing for calculating that the Qur'an was magic rather than poetry or soothsaying.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p141/r13.anchor: أي لعن ثم لعن كيف قدر أنه ليس بشعر ولا كهانة , وأنه سحر

BURSEVI:v10p177/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p177/r1.claim: Taqdir means measuring, arranging, and preparing; the man considered what to say to attack the Quran and rehearsed it within himself.

BURSEVI:v10p177/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p177/r2.claim: The phrase marvels at his calculation as if it hit the Quraysh's target, though calling the Quran magic is a feeble and absurd conclusion.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r2.anchor: تعجيب من تقديره وإصابته فيه الغرض الذي كان ينتحيه قريش قاتلهم الله

BURSEVI:v10p177/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p177/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase mocks Quraysh for quoting the curse and admiring their own estimate; 'May God kill him' can express astonishment at extreme skill in poetry or bravery.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r3.anchor: أو حكاية لما ذكروه من قولهم قتل كيف قدر تهكما بهم وبإعجابهم بتقديره

BURSEVI:v10p177/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p177/r4.claim: He points back to his fuller explanation of the idiom 'May God fight them' in the sura al-Munafiqun.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r4.anchor: وقد سبق في قاتلهم الله في المنافقين مزيد البيان

BURSEVI:v10p177/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r5.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
BURSEVI:v10p177/r5.claim: Walid heard the Prophet reciting al-Sajda, or according to some commentaries the opening of Ha Mim al-Mumin, and told Banu Makhzum the speech was neither human nor jinn.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r5.anchor: إن الوليد مر بالنبي عليه السلام وهو يقر أحم السجدة وفي بعض التفاسير فواتح سورة حم المؤمن

BURSEVI:v10p177/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r6.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
BURSEVI:v10p177/r6.claim: Walid praised the Quran's sweetness and beauty, saying its top bore fruit and its bottom flowed abundantly, like a fresh, well-rooted tree.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r6.anchor: والله لقد سمعت من محمد آنفا كلاما ما هو من كلام الأنس ولا من كلام الجن إن له لحلاوة وإن عليه لطلاوة

BURSEVI:v10p177/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p177/r7.claim: The Quran is likened to a verdant tree with a strong root, fruitful upper branches, and a richly watered lower part.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r7.anchor: شبه القرآن بالشجرة الغضة الطرية التي استحكم أصلها بكثرة الماء وأثمرت فروعها في السماء

BURSEVI:v10p177/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v10p177/r8.claim: Kashifi's Persian rendering describes the Quran as uniquely sweet and fresh, with fruits of complete felicity above and roots of virtues and wisdom below.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r8.anchor: مراورا حلاوتي وعذوبتي هست كه هي سخن رانباشد وبروى طر أوتى وتازكي هست كه هي حديثي رانبود

BURSEVI:v10p177/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r9.speaker: قريش
BURSEVI:v10p177/r9.claim: When Walid said the Quran triumphs and cannot be surpassed, Quraysh accused him of apostasy; Abu Jahl offered to deal with him and approached him while he sat grieving.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r9.anchor: ثم قال الوليد وإنه يعلو ولا يعلى فقالت قريش صبأ والله الوليد أي مال عن دينه

BURSEVI:v10p177/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r10.speaker: أبو جهل
BURSEVI:v10p177/r10.claim: Abu Jahl accused Walid of praising Muhammad to curry favor for food scraps; Walid answered that Quraysh had wealth and Muhammad's followers were too poor to feed anyone.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r10.anchor: توسخنان محمدا عليه السلام سند ميدهى وآنرا بزرك ميدارى وثنا ميكويى تا از فضله طعام ايشان بهره بردارى

BURSEVI:v10p177/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p177/r11.speaker: الوليد بن المغيرة
BURSEVI:v10p177/r11.claim: Walid told Quraysh that Muhammad's reputation had spread among Arabs and the pilgrimage season was near, so they needed to agree what answer to give visitors.
BURSEVI:v10p177/r11.anchor: بدانيدكه حال وكار اين محمد در عرب منتشر كشت وموسم حج نزديكست كه عرب مى آيند وازحال وى رسند

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#8/r1.anchor: ﴿ فقتل ﴾ لعن ﴿ كيف قدر ﴾ تعجيب من تقديره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p295#8/r2.claim: The phrase expresses amazement at his estimation and plotting.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r4.claim: The author first glosses qutila as a curse.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r4.anchor: { فقتل } أي لعن. وكان بعض أهل التأويل يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r5.speaker: بعض أهل التأويل
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r5.claim: Some interpreters say qutila means he was subdued or overcome; anything subdued can be called maqtul.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:18/r5.anchor: وكان بعض أهل التأويل يقول: معناها فقهر وغلب، وكل مذلل مقتل قال الشاعر:

QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r1.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r1.claim: Al-Zuhri glosses qutila as “he was punished,” in the form of a curse.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r1.anchor: وقال الزهري: عذب وهو من باب الدعاء. { كيف قدر }

QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r2.speaker: ناس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r2.claim: Some take kayfa as an expression of amazement, like “How did you do this?”; the author connects it with 25:9.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r2.anchor: قال ناس: «كيف» تعجيب كما يقال للرجل تتعجب من صنيعه: كيف فعلت هذا؟

QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r3.speaker: قوم
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r3.claim: Another view reads the question literally: in what manner did al-Walid calculate his claim?
QURTUBI-FULL:74:19-22/r3.anchor: { كيف قدر } أي على أي حال قدر.

RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r1.claim: The formula is used for amazement and magnification, as in proverbial curses that exclaim how courageous or eloquent someone is.
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r1.anchor: وهذا إنما يذكر عند التعجب والاستعظام ، ومثله قولهم : قتله الله ما أشجعه

RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r2.claim: One possible reading marvels at the strength of his thinking: he could not have devised a stronger or greater doubt against Muhammad.
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r2.anchor: أنه تعجيب من قوة خاطره ، يعني أنه لا يمكن القدح في أمر محمد عليه السلام بشبهة أعظم

RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is sarcastic praise: what he proposed was extremely feeble and worthless.
RAZI-FULL:v30p177/r3.anchor: الثناء عليه على طريقة الاستهزاء ، يعني أن هذا الذي ذكره في غاية الركاكة والسقوط

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r1.claim: The solitary man pondered what to say about the Qur'an; the author glosses f-qutila as a curse on his calculation, then says he reconsidered, pinched his brow, and grimaced.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r1.anchor: يقول: ثم لعن كيف قدر النازل فيه

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.claim: Ikrima recounts that al-Walid ibn al-Mughira was moved by Muhammad's recitation and praised its sweetness and force, but after Abu Jahl pressured him to oppose it he decided to call it magic inherited from another; the passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة أن الوليد بن المغيرة جاء إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فقرأ عليه القرآن، فكأنه رق له

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r4.claim: Qatada says al-Walid was created alone from his mother's womb and that the revelation then ran through the verse about nineteen.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r4.anchor: قال قتادة: خرج من بطن أمه وحيدا، فنزلت هذه الآية حتى بلغ {تسعة عشر} [المدثر: 30]

TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that al-Walid first told Quraysh the Qur'an was God's speech, not poetry, magic, or madness; fearing his conversion, Abu Jahl shamed him into calling it magic acquired from others, and the passage was revealed.
TAB-FULL:v23p428/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إنه فكر وقدر} [المدثر: 18] إلى {ثم عبس وبسر} [المدثر: 22] قال: دخل الوليد بن المغيرة على أبي بكر

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r1.claim: Qatada reports al-Walid saying the Qur'an was not poetry, had sweetness and surpassing beauty, yet must be magic; he then frowned and grimaced, prompting the curse in the verse.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {إنه فكر وقدر} [المدثر: 18] زعموا أنه قال: والله لقد نظرت فيما قال هذا الرجل

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the solitary one as al-Walid, whom Muhammad invited to Islam; after delaying, considering, frowning, turning away, and calling the message magic, he was consigned to Saqar.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r3.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا} [المدثر: 11] يعني الوليد بن المغيرة دعاه نبي الله

TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that al-Walid examined Muhammad reciting in prayer, called the speech sweet and heart-gripping, rejected poetry and soothsaying, then allowed that it might be magic transmitted from earlier people.
TAB-FULL:v23p431/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ذرني ومن خلقت وحيدا وجعلت له مالا ممدودا} [المدثر: 12] إلى قوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r1.claim: Fa-qutila is a curse; al-Wāḥidī refers to the same usage in 51:10 and 9:30.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r1.anchor: لعن؛ وذكرنا ذلك عند قوله: {قتل الخراصون} (¬1) و {قاتلهم الله أنى يؤفكون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r2.claim: The verse-arrangement commentator says the phrase may attach to what precedes: he was cursed in whatever way he calculated, like saying I will kill him however he acts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r2.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: يجوز أن يكون هذا منتظما بما قبله على معنى: فلعن على أي حال قدر ما قدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r3.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r3.claim: Alternatively, the phrase begins a new sentence of rebuke and amazement, since the preceding sentence is complete, like asking someone who did wrong how he could do it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p428/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون منقطعا بما قبله مستأنفا؛ لأنه لما قال: {إنه فكر وقدر (18) فقتل}، كان هذا تماما

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r1.claim: The author defines takrār as repeating or restoring something, a verbal noun on tafʿāl with an open tāʾ, an irregular pattern unlike tafʿīl.
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r1.anchor: التكرار على وجه التأكيد وهو مصدر كرر إذا ردد وأعاد هو تفعال بفتح التاء وليس بقياس بخلاف التفعيل

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r2.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r2.claim: The Kufans analyze takrār as a verbal noun of faʿala, with its alif replacing the yāʾ in tafʿīl.
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r2.anchor: وقال الكوفيون هو مصدر فعل والألف عوض من الياء في التفعيل

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r3.speaker: سيبويه
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r3.claim: The author prefers Sibawayh's analysis: takrār is tafʿāl, an irregular verbal noun unlike tafʿīl.
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r3.anchor: وقال الكوفيون هو مصدر فعل والألف عوض من الياء في التفعيل والأول مذهب سيبويه

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r4.claim: The author rejects the claim that repetition lacks eloquence: Arabs repeat an obscure matter to confirm it, signal its nearness, or intensify a curse.
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r4.anchor: وقد غلط من أنكر كونه من أساليب الفصاحة ظنا أنه لا فائدة له وليس كذلك بل هو من محاسنها

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r5.claim: Repetition can stand in for an oath or for intense supplication against someone; Qur'anic speech uses the Arabs' own rhetorical habits to establish their inability to match it.
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r5.anchor: إذ أبهمت بشيء إرادة لتحقيقه وقرب وقوعه أو قصدت الدعاء عليه كررته توكيدا وكأنها تقيم تكراره مقام المقسم عليه

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r6.claim: Repeated admonitions, promises, and threats answer human beings' varied dispositions and persistent desires; the author invokes the Qur'an's being made easy for remembrance.
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r6.anchor: وعلى ذلك يحتمل ما ورد من تكرار المواعظ والوعد والوعيد لأن الإنسان مجبول من الطبائع المختلفة

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r8.claim: The author gives paired repetitions as examples, including the doubled curse in this verse and repeated warnings, promises, and denials elsewhere.

BURHAN:v3p8#2/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r9.claim: The chief purpose of repetition is confirmation: as the saying goes, speech becomes established when repeated.
BURHAN:v3p8#2/r9.anchor: وقد قيل الكلام إذا تكرر تقرر

BURHAN:v3p18/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p18/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p18/r1.claim: The repeated curse expresses amazement at his calculation and his having hit the mark, like the Arabic exclamation, May God curse him, how brave he is.
BURHAN:v3p18/r1.anchor: فأعيد تعجبا من تقديره وإصابته الغرض على حد قاتله الله ما أشجعه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p97/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p97/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p97/r1.claim: In reporting that a seemingly harmless man killed someone, placing the killer first highlights the surprising fact that this unlikely agent acted; the novelty lies in who killed, not who was killed.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p97/r1.anchor: ذاك لأن الذي يعنيه ويعني الناس من شأن هذا القتل طرافته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p97/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p97/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p97/r2.claim: It is insufficient to say an element was fronted for emphasis; the analyst must explain why it matters. Neglecting such rhetorical distinctions obscures eloquence and inimitability, unlike focusing only on sound details such as أأنذرتهم, imāla, and الصراط/الزراط.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p97/r2.anchor: وقد وقع في ظنون الناس أنه يكفي أن يقال : إنه قدم للعناية

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r1.claim: With لم يأتني القوم كلهم, the negative applies to the whole group, so some may have come; with كلهم لم يأتني, it applies to each one, making the claim that some came contradictory.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r1.anchor: لم يأتني القوم كلهم ، ولكن أتاني بعضهم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r2.claim: The semantic difference does not truly arise from whether كل is governed by the verb; it arises from whether كل falls within the scope of negation, as the separable negator ما shows.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r2.anchor: وهو دخول كل في حيز النفي

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r3.claim: The two cited poems, ما كل ما يتمنى المرء يدركه and ما كل رأي الفتى يدعو إلى رشد, illustrate that كل remains within negation even when not governed by the verb; fronting كل outside negation instead denies any instance.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p218/r3.anchor: ما كل رأي الفتى يدعو إلى رشد

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r17.claim: Qutila literally means “slain”; applied to the still-living al-Walīd it implies spiritual death, and is glossed as accursed or punished.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r17.anchor: Perish translates qutila, which literally means “slain,”

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r18.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r18.claim: The repeated curse may mean al-Walīd determined his own fate by how he judged the Prophet’s nature.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r18.anchor: the fact that al-Walīd determined his own fate by the manner in which he sought to determine the nature of the Prophet

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r19.speaker: Bg
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r19.claim: The repeated wording can serve as emphasis.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r19.anchor: the repetition can be seen as emphasis

STUDYQURAN:74:11/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r20.claim: The repetition may instead indicate punishment, perishing, or death in both this life and the next.
STUDYQURAN:74:11/r20.anchor: al-Walīd would be punished, perish, or be slain in both this life and the next

TABATABAI:74:12-25/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r8.claim: Al-Walid sought a claim that would undermine the Qurʾan and satisfy its hostile opponents; after considering poetry, soothsaying, madness, and fables, he chose magic because it divides families and allies.
TABATABAI:74:12-25/r8.anchor: وقد كان الرجل يهوى أن يقول في أمر القرآن شيئا يبطل به دعوته ويرضي به قومه المعاندين

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r14.claim: He reasoned that calling the Qurʾān poetry would be rejected by Arabs and calling it soothsaying would fail because it resembles no soothsayer's speech, so he chose sorcery attributed to other magicians.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r14.anchor: إن قلنا شاعر كذبتنا العرب باعتبار ما أتى به وإن قلنا كاهن لم يصدقونا

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r15.claim: The curse formula means that he was cursed and tormented.

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r16.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r16.claim: An alternative takes the curse as one that is comparable to killing.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r16.anchor: وقيل: لعن بما يجري مجرى القتل

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r17.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r17.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the man deserved punishment.

TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r18.speaker: صاحب النظم
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r18.claim: The phrase means he was cursed whatever way he calculated his words, like saying someone will be struck however he acts.
TABRISI:74:11-31#2/r18.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: معناه لعن على أي حال قدر ما قدر من الكلام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r10.claim: “Faqutila” means cursed and punished; “how did he determine?” is an expression of astonishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:11-19/r10.anchor: { فقتل } لعن وعذب { كيف قدر }؟ استفهام على طريق التعجب.

ELMALILI:74:14-25/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r12.claim: Qutila and qatalahu Allah are curses, but can also express admiration; here the phrase mocks those praising al-Walid's calculation by echoing their praise contemptuously.
ELMALILI:74:14-25/r12.anchor: burada onun düşüncesini beğenenlerin bu yoldaki senâlarını hikâye ile tahkir içindir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.claim: Verses 18–25 condemn people who, like al-Walīd, adopt a similar unbelieving posture toward the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r3.anchor: İşte 18-25. âyetlerde Velîd b. Mug^re örneğinde Kur’an’a karşı benzer şekilde inkârcı tutum sergileyenler kınanmış

DAMGHANI:v1p371/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r2.claim: Qutila can be a curse or imprecation, as in the curse against the makers of the trench.
DAMGHANI:v1p371/r2.anchor: الثالث القتل اللعن قوله تعالى في سورة المدثر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r8.claim: Qatl can be a curse or imprecation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p494#2/r8.anchor: والثالث : اللعن . ومنه قوله تعالى في الذاريات

FARRA:v3p202/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p202/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p202/r1.claim: When Meccan leaders debated what to tell pilgrims, al-Walid rejected calling Muhammad mad, poet, or soothsayer; after deliberation he chose to call him a sorcerer.
FARRA:v3p202/r1.anchor: فهذا تفسير قوله: «إنه فكر وقدر» القول فى محمد صلى الله عليه

FARRA:v3p202/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p202/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p202/r2.claim: قتل means may he be cursed, as in قاتلهم الله and قتل الإنسان ما أكفره.
FARRA:v3p202/r2.anchor: قتل أي: لعن، وكذلك: «قاتلهم الله » و «قتل الإنسان ما أكفره »

NAHHAS:v5p67/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r3.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p67/r3.anchor: قال أبو جعفر قول الفراء قتل بمعنى لعن

NAHHAS:v5p67/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p67/r4.claim: Arabic usage requires قتل to mean ‘destroyed,’ since a killed person is destroyed.
NAHHAS:v5p67/r4.anchor: هذا يجب على كلام العرب أن يكون قتل بمعنى أهلك لأن المقتول مهلك

ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.claim: On hearing the messages, he reflects on how to disprove them, destroys himself by that deliberation, looks for arguments, frowns, then turns away and glories in arrogance.
ASAD-NOTES:74:16/r3.anchor: he reflects and meditates [as to how to disprove them]

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r1.claim: Qutila means he was cursed; kayfa qaddara expresses astonishment, rejection, and reproach.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r1.anchor: {فقتل} لعن، وقال الزهري: عذب، {كيف قدر} على طريق التعجب والإنكار والتوبيخ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r2.speaker: الزهري
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r2.anchor: وقال الزهري: عذب، {كيف قدر} على طريق التعجب والإنكار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r3.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r3.claim: Most exegetes take the repeated formula as a curse on al-Walid and condemnation of his judgment, declaring him deserving of it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r3.anchor: فقتل كيف قدر ثم قتل كيف قدر هو دعاء عليه وتقبيح لحاله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r4.claim: Alternatively, the apparent curse can praise al-Walid's initial judgment and sound denial that the Quran was poetry, soothsaying, or madness; Arabs use such curse formulas approvingly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r4.anchor: فيحتمل قوله تعالى: فقتل كيف قدر أن يكون دعاء عليه على معنى تقبيح حاله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r5.claim: He illustrates approving curse language with the Prophet's remark about Abu Jandal and Abd al-Malik's قاتل الله كثيرا; this is familiar Arab usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395/r5.anchor: قول عبد الملك بن مروان: قاتل الله كثيرا كأنه رآنا حين قال كذا

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.claim: The passage is said to concern al-Walid ibn al-Mughira al-Makhzumi, wealthy with sons and called al-Wahid among his people, according to Ibn Amir.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r10.anchor: قيل: نزلت هذه الآيات في الوليد بن المغيرة المخزومي، وكان له مال وبنون، قال ابن عامر: وكان يسمى الوحيد في قومه،

JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.claim: In the story, al-Walid rejects calling Muhammad a soothsayer, poet, or madman, then chooses “magician” and says the Qur’an separates families.
JISHUMI:v10p7156/r11.anchor: ثم اختلفوا، فقيل: إنه أتى قريشا في ناديها، وقال: هذا الموسم، والناس يسألون عن محمد،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r7.claim: The words may express astonishment that his calculation struck Quraysh's intended target.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r7.anchor: تعجيب من تقديره وإصابته فيه المحز

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r8.claim: Alternatively, the apparent praise is sarcastic, or quotes Quraysh's repeated taunt to mock their admiration.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r9.claim: The idiom قتله الله ما أشجعه conveys that someone has reached a remarkable level that would make an envious person curse him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p650/r9.anchor: ومعنى قول القائل : قتله الله ما أشجعه

MUQATIL:74:18-30/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r2.claim: Fa-qutila is a curse directed at al-Walid for reckoning Muhammad's message to be sorcery.
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r2.anchor: { فقتل } يقول: فلعن { كيف قدر } [آية: 19] السحر
